rows.description: Create and subsidize paid internships and structured work placements embedded in vocational and university programmes, with formal agreements between education institutions and employers to ensure relevant experience on graduation.
rows.citizen_demand: More and better-regulated paid internships and closer collaboration between education and companies so graduates gain relevant experience.
rows.priority_justification: Frequent, high-relevance mentions across education and employment categories; several respondents explicitly propose paid internships and curricular company collaboration; sentiment mixes hope and frustration.
rows.title: Expand paid, work-integrated internships and stronger education–business collaboration
rows.sentiment_context: Predominantly constructive but urgent: respondents express hope for better school–company links and paid internships, with medium sentiment intensity.

rows.description: Establish targeted measures (e.g., hiring subsidies, funded trainee positions, probation rules) to encourage employers to offer positions that do not require prior experience and to provide on-the-job training for young hires.
rows.citizen_demand: Help companies hire inexperienced young people through subsidies, trainee schemes and regulated on-the-job training so youth can build experience.
rows.priority_justification: Widespread, strongly felt barrier (many high experience_barrier scores); multiple explicit proposals for subsidies/entry jobs across responses.
rows.title: Create entry-level job pathways and incentives for firms to hire inexperienced youth
rows.sentiment_context: Negative to frustrated: many respondents report being blocked by experience requirements; proposals combine criticism with constructive remedies.

rows.description: Introduce clearer regulations for internships and practice agreements (including minimum pay and limits on unpaid work) and put measures to reduce excessive use of temporary contracts and unpredictable extra hours.
rows.citizen_demand: Better regulation of internships (remuneration and access) and limits on temporary contracts and abusive working hours.
rows.priority_justification: Repeated, emotionally charged reports about precarious internships and temporary contracts; several explicit calls for regulatory action.
rows.title: Regulate internships and limit precarious temporary-contract practices
rows.sentiment_context: Negative, medium–high intensity: respondents express frustration with unpaid/temporary offers and exploitation of inexperienced workers.

rows.description: Promote transparent hiring processes (reduce reliance on informal contacts), create youth-targeted employment pools or specialized job boards, accept portfolios or demonstrable skills in public hiring, and consider temporary prioritization mechanisms for younger applicants.
rows.citizen_demand: Fairer, more transparent hiring: reduce contact-based selection, create youth job pools/specialized boards, and allow portfolios as proof of competence.
rows.priority_justification: Recurring complaints about contact-based hiring and non-response, combined with several explicit proposals (job pools, quotas, portfolio recognition) indicate high analytical relevance.
rows.title: Improve recruitment transparency and broaden recognition of alternative credentials
rows.sentiment_context: Critical and solution-oriented: respondents express frustration at non-transparent hiring and propose concrete institutional fixes (job pools, portfolio acceptance); sentiment intensity medium–high.

rows.description: Provide formal career-orientation services inside educational institutions (vocational and higher education) that inform students about labour-market demands, opportunities, and pathways to gain experience.
rows.citizen_demand: More and earlier orientation for students from their own institutions to understand labour-market options and how to access them.
rows.priority_justification: Common and actionable demand but less emotionally intense than experience/contract issues; recurring across education levels.
rows.title: Strengthen career guidance and student orientation within education institutions
rows.sentiment_context: Hopeful and corrective: respondents request guidance to reduce uncertainty and mismatches; sentiment intensity medium.

rows.description: Support measures to decentralize industry and create regional job opportunities (e.g., incentives for firms to locate outside big cities) and improve transport/organizational arrangements (including vocational calendar alignment) to reduce commuting barriers to sector jobs.
rows.citizen_demand: More regional job creation, transport solutions and vocational-timing adjustments so local graduates can access real hiring opportunities without relocating.
rows.priority_justification: Frequent in certain sectors/regions with high relevance where respondents report concrete transport and locality problems; sentiment medium.
rows.title: Address regional barriers: decentralize opportunities and improve mobility for sector jobs
rows.sentiment_context: Negative/concerned: respondents describe geographic isolation of jobs and transport hardship; propose decentralization and calendar adjustments with medium intensity.

rows.description: Consider measures to improve pay conditions for entry-level jobs and ensure internships/practices provide at least minimum remuneration—actions may include wage regulation discussions, targeted subsidies, or sectoral agreements to align pay with qualification and living costs.
rows.citizen_demand: Regulate or support wages so jobs and internships pay adequately and enable financial independence.
rows.priority_justification: Repeated concern about pay across respondents, but policy specifics vary; emotional intensity is significant though fewer explicit, detailed proposals than for experience barriers.
rows.title: Actions to address low pay and ensure adequate remuneration for youth
rows.sentiment_context: Negative and concerned: respondents often link low pay to inability to be independent and to exploitation of inexperienced hires; sentiment intensity medium–high.

rows.description: Increase or time competitive public-sector hiring (oposiciones) and adapt public recruitment criteria to allow demonstration of skills (e.g., portfolios) to open stable entry-level positions for young people.
rows.citizen_demand: Convene public competitive calls and open hiring routes that allow capable young applicants (not only those with formal credentials) to obtain stable jobs.
rows.priority_justification: High relevance for some respondents and explicit proposals present, though support is concentrated in a subset of responses.
rows.title: Create stable public-sector entry points (targeted public hiring)
rows.sentiment_context: Critical of current public hiring but pragmatic: respondents see public-sector vacancies as an avenue for stable employment and request broader access criteria.

rows.description: Offer targeted supports (training, financial incentives, incubators) to encourage young entrepreneurship and measures to incentivize firms to create stable positions for young people.
rows.citizen_demand: More support for entrepreneurship and incentives for companies to expand hiring so youth can create or find local opportunities.
rows.priority_justification: Present in the dataset but less frequent than core issues (experience, internships, temporary contracts); nonetheless relevant as a complementary pathway.
rows.title: Support youth entrepreneurship and incentives for job creation
rows.sentiment_context: Constructive and hopeful: respondents propose entrepreneurship as an alternative given scarce local opportunities; sentiment intensity medium.
